memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For no one has ever shown the mighty power or performed the awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel." — Deut 34:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Torah — the first five books of the Bible — comes to its close with these words honouring Moses' mighty power and awesome deeds. It is a fitting end to the life of a truly great servant of God. Yet the way it ends leaves us with a sense of anticipation. The final verses declare that no prophet has arisen like Moses — and this quietly reminds us of God's earlier promise that one day a Prophet like Moses would come (Deut 18:15). The story is not finished. Something greater is still ahead.

This is how the whole Old Testament works. It is full of great figures and mighty acts, yet it always points beyond itself, leaving us longing for someone greater. Moses was a mighty deliverer who led God's people out of slavery in Egypt. But even he could not bring them all the way in, and even his glory was a shadow of a greater glory to come.

That greater Deliverer is Jesus Christ. Moses led Israel out of bondage to Pharaoh; Jesus leads His people out of bondage to sin and death. Moses gave the law; Jesus fulfilled it and brought grace and truth (John 1:17). Moses was a faithful servant in God's house; Jesus is the Son over God's house (Heb 3:5-6). Where Moses could only point the way, Christ is the way.

So as we close this great book, we lift our eyes to the One it was always preparing us to see. The mighty deeds of Moses stir our hearts, but they were signposts to Jesus, the greater Prophet, the greater Deliverer, the Son who brings us all the way home to God. He is the One in whom the whole story finds its meaning. Look to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see how the Old Testament points forward to Christ?
2. How is Jesus a greater Deliverer than even Moses?
3. What does it mean to look to Christ as the One the whole story prepares us for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the mighty works of Moses, and thank You even more for Jesus, the greater Deliverer they pointed to. As I close this book, lift my eyes to Christ, in whom the whole story finds its meaning. Amen.
